title: First Missing Positive
prompt: Given an unsorted integer array `nums`, return the smallest missing positive integer. You must implement an algorithm that runs in `O(n)` time and uses `O(1)` auxiliary space.
hints: Sorting first gives an easy O(n log n) solution, and a hash set gives O(n) time but O(n) space — the O(1) space requirement means you need to reuse the array itself as your data structure.
The answer must be in the range [1, n+1], since there are only n slots — if all of 1..n are present, the answer is n+1.
Use cyclic sort: place each value v (where 1 <= v <= n) at index v-1 by repeatedly swapping it into position; afterward, scan for the first index i where nums[i] != i+1 — that index+1 is the answer.

solution.approach: The answer must lie in [1, n+1] since there are only n elements. Use cyclic sort: for each position, if the value there is in range [1, n] and not already at its correct home (index value-1), swap it into that home position, repeating until the current position holds a correctly-placed value or an out-of-range one. After this pass, every value v in [1, n] that exists in the array sits at index v-1. A final scan finds the first index i where nums[i] != i+1; that i+1 is the first missing positive. If every index matches, the answer is n+1. Each element is swapped at most once into its final home, keeping the whole process O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
